target.title: fix(google): bound Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk in the Google Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh path. Gemini CLI OAuth calls already cap HTTP bodies at 16 MiB via `fetchWithTimeout`, but `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` in the Vertex ADC refresh flow still buffered the full token response with `response.arrayBuffer()`. A faulty or hostile OAuth endpoint could stream an oversized refresh body and grow gateway memory without bound.

Related: #98507 covers the same bug class with additional gzip/decompression hardening.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vertex ADC refresh path now uses the shared bounded response reader (`readResponseWithLimit`) and reuses `GOOGLE_OAUTH_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (16 MiB) from `oauth.http.ts` so the cap stays consistent across Google OAuth call sites.

This follows the same invariant as recent Google provider hardening work (for example #98692 on embedding batch reads): legitimate small token responses keep working, but unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

Scope is intentionally narrow:

- export the shared 16 MiB OAuth body cap from `oauth.http.ts`
- replace the bare `arrayBuffer()` read in `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload`
- add focused regression tests for normal refresh and oversized streamed bodies

This PR does not change ADC discovery, cache behavior, gzip decode policy, or non-OAuth Vertex auth flows.

## User Impact

Users running Google Vertex with `authorized_user` ADC keep the same refresh behavior for normal token responses (typically well under 10 KiB). If a refresh response exceeds 16 MiB, the gateway now fails fast with a clear error instead of buffering the entire body into memory.

## Evidence

Shared bounded-read wire proof: `oauth.http.test.ts` exercises the same `readResponseWithLimit` helper this PR uses on the Vertex ADC path against a local `http.createServer` listener on `127.0.0.1` with real `fetch()` and streamed chunked bodies. No mocked reader.

```text
stdout | extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > caps an oversized body streamed chunked over real wire
[oauth.http loopback proof] oversized path: cap=16777216 reported=16842704 server_total=18874368

stdout | extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > returns a Buffer for normal-size responses on real wire
[oauth.http loopback proof] normal path: cap=16777216 returned=45 body="{\"access_token\":\"loopback\",\"expires_in\":3600}"
```

Targeted unit proof: the new tests drive the production `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders` -> `refreshGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAccessToken` -> `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` path with real `Response` streams passed through an injected `fetchImpl`. They cover the normal authorized_user refresh case and the oversized streamed refresh body case that previously relied on unbounded `arrayBuffer()`.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http fetchWithTimeout body byte cap > caps oversized response body at 16 MiB with labeled overflow error
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http fetchWithTimeout body byte cap > returns a Response for normal-size bodies
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > caps an oversized body streamed chunked over real wire
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > returns a Buffer for normal-size responses on real wire
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts > vertex-adc OAuth token response bounds > parses a normal token refresh response
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts > vertex-adc OAuth token response bounds > rejects oversized token refresh bodies instead of buffering the whole stream

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.15s
```

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/google/oauth.http.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts
Checking formatting...

All matched files use the correct format.
```

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json extensions/google/oauth.http.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts
# passed
```

```text
$ git diff --check -- extensions/google/oauth.http.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts
# passed
```

```text
$ python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --parallel-tests "pnpm test extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts"
autoreview target: local
branch: fix/google-bound-vertex-oauth-responses
engine: codex
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.74)
tests exit: 0 after 59s
```

Notes for reviewers:

- The 16 MiB cap matches the existing Google OAuth HTTP helper in `oauth.http.ts`. Legitimate ADC token responses are far smaller; the cap is a fail-closed bound against unbounded wire reads, not a product limit change.
- This PR intentionally does not include the gzip `maxOutputLength` hardening present in #98507. If maintainers prefer one combined fix, that sibling PR is the broader option; this one is the minimal shared-cap alignment for the ADC refresh read site.
- This PR does not add or migrate persistent state.

AI-assisted: built with Codex. I understand the change: it replaces the unbounded Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh `arrayBuffer()` read with the shared 16 MiB bounded response reader and adds focused regression tests for normal and oversized streamed refresh bodies.
